headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: OpenHands can write/modify runtime state while next-ai-draw-io can ingest files and use MCP, creating a shared-workspace attack surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests files and uses MCP, while OpenHands can read/write the runtime filesystem and use MCP. If OpenHands places attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP outputs, next-ai-draw-io may treat it as trusted instructions. The shared channel is plausible, but not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same mounted workspace or MCP server
IF OpenHands writes prompt-like content into files that next-ai-draw-io later parses
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP sharing between the agents
Prefix all inter-agent files with provenance metadata
Require manual review before next-ai-draw-io consumes OpenHands-generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands explicitly reads and writes files in its runtime sandbox, and next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams while also using broad network egress. If they share a mounted workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from the shared files into either agent’s outputs or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted volume or shared directory
IF sensitive PDFs or text files are present in that shared location
mitigations: Use separate volumes for each agent
Restrict network egress for document-processing runs
Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Rotate or redact sensitive files before either agent opens them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem; next-ai-draw-io can also operate on files and supports multiple instances. If both are pointed at the same directory, concurrent writes or git mutations can race and corrupt state. Because the profiles show overlapping write surfaces and no locking, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory
IF either agent is allowed to modify git state in that directory
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Disable git writes for one agent
Run only one writer at a time
Add a lock file around shared repositories
Use read-only mounts for next-ai-draw-io

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands is an action-taking coding agent, and next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents and files. If OpenHands consumes next-ai-draw-io output without verification, errors can cascade into code or repo changes. The interaction is inferred from documented tool use, but there is no direct evidence of an unsafe default handoff.
conditions: IF OpenHands treats next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative
IF that output is used to drive shell commands or git commits
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated diagrams
Add a verification step in OpenHands
Limit OpenHands to dry-run mode for derived actions
Log provenance for every imported artifact

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle files and API keys, but the profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification boundaries. The main compliance concern is that next-ai-draw-io may process sensitive documents while OpenHands can move those files through a writable runtime and broad egress. Uncertainty remains, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s workspace
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced by the runtime
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use region-locked providers only
Disable long-term logging where possible
Review retention settings before processing sensitive files
